chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdullah al-Mu'min, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Which is worse, adultery or drinking wine?' And 'How did it come to be that the penalty for wine is eighty lashes and for adultery is one hundred?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Is'haq! The penalty (hadd) is one, but this was increased because of the wasting of the sperm and placing it in other than its rightful place, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the lash penalty for wine drinking different from that of adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while the foundational legal status of *zina* (adultery) and *shurb al-khamr* (wine drinking) shares a common basis, the specific penalty of eighty lashes for wine is elevated due to the unique harm of wasting the seed (*nutfa*) in an improper place. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the preservation of lineage and the specific physiological consequences of intoxication, distinguishing it from the broader category of illicit sexual union.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah Al Razy, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdullah Al Momin, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Is the adulterer more evil or drinker of the wine? And how did eighty lashes come to be with regards to the wine, and a hundred regarding adultery?’ So heasws said: ‘O Is’haq! The Penalty (Hadd) is one, but there is an increase in this due to his wasting of the sperm and placing it in other than its (rightful) place which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Commanded it with’.
